title: A Static for the Gravity
premise: Coral Eriksen has spent eleven years alone on Kepler-442c tending a seed vault garden for colonists who will never arrive, her only companion the beacon she maintains out of stubborn habit. When gravity stutters system-wide for nine seconds, the beacon wakes and reveals it was built by Coral's long-disappeared mother as a dead-man's switch carrying proof that the war between Earth and the Belt was manufactured by the terraforming consortium. Hunted by consortium agents and shadowed by a defector pilot named Juno, Coral must carry the message to the neutral relay at Ceres before the consortium's final strike — discovering along the way that 'found family' is not a consolation but a weapon. She delivers the message, but at the cost of the beacon's destruction and her own near-death; the war ends not with victory but with both sides forced to inherit the same uncomfortable truth.
about_author: Paloma Vasquez is a former botanist who spent six years working in closed-ecosystem research facilities in the Atacama before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for their quiet characters, botanical precision, and the conviction that tenderness is a form of resistance.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On an ordinary morning tending the seed vault, gravity across the system flickers for exactly nine seconds, and every plant in the garden rises like startled birds. When the beacon she has maintained for years begins transmitting on its own, Coral realizes it was never hers to maintain. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Garden for Nobody
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter in Coral's POV establishing her eleven years of solitude: the seed vault commissioned by a colony ship that never came, and the routine rituals that keep loneliness at bay. She decodes the beacon's first fragment and finds her mother's handwriting in the metadata. Emotional beat: grief rediscovered as inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Beacon Remembers
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The beacon's archive unspools partially corrupted logs: her mother Ada Eriksen helped design it as a failsafe containing evidence of a fabricated provocation that started the Earth–Belt war. A consortium survey drone enters orbit. Emotional beat: the past arriving with teeth.

chapters.title: Juno Descending
chapters.summary: POV shift to Juno Okonkwo, a disgraced Belt pilot shot down over Kepler-442c while fleeing consortium pursuit. She crash-lands near the garden and is taken in at gunpoint by Coral. Two wary women circle each other over freeze-dried tea. Emotional beat: distrust as a first language.

chapters.title: Terms of Shelter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Negotiation: Juno offers passage to Ceres in exchange for the message; Coral refuses to hand over her mother's work to a stranger. The drone deploys hunter probes into the atmosphere. They fight off the first probe together, badly. Emotional beat: necessity forging an uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: Ada's Voice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A repaired log plays Ada's personal addendum, meant only for her daughter: an apology, an explanation of why she vanished, and a warning that the consortium will come wearing friendly faces. Coral rages at being made an heir to a war. Emotional beat: anger as a form of love.

chapters.title: Liftoff from a Dead World
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. They strip the garden's power systems to fuel Juno's crippled ship, the Long Patience. Coral seals the greenhouse, leaving her life's work behind under automated care. Liftoff through the probe net is violent and costly — the ship loses its long-range antenna. Emotional beat: leaving home as amputation.

chapters.title: The Quiet Between Burns
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating in short sections. In transit, the two women trade histories: Juno lost her crew to a consortium false-flag attack; Coral lost everyone by never having them. Small domestic rituals form aboard ship — shared meals, watch rotations. Emotional beat: found family beginning as habit.

chapters.title: Intercept at the Fuel Ghost
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. A refueling stop at an abandoned mining platform becomes an ambush by consortium agent Marek Voss, who offers Coral amnesty and her mother's sealed personnel file if she surrenders the beacon core. They escape, but Coral glimpses her mother's file: listed as deceased, twelve years ago. Emotional beat: hope weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Dead Twelve Years
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral spirals — if Ada died twelve years ago, who programmed the beacon's recent transmissions? Juno suggests the truth: the beacon is autonomous, carrying out its dead creator's instructions, and one transmission remains unsent. Coral must choose to finish what a dead woman started. Emotional beat: despair transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Belt's Open Hand
chapters.summary: New POV: Ambassador Sefu Ndiaye aboard the Belt flagship Meridian, receiving intercepted fragments of the beacon signal and realizing what Ada Eriksen's evidence could do — or destroy. He dispatches ships toward Ceres, unsure whether to protect the courier or silence her. Emotional beat: institutional fear dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Slingshot
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. To reach Ceres before the consortium fleet, they attempt a dangerous gravity-assist through Jupiter's magnetosphere, using the nine-second anomaly data as a navigation key — the flicker was Ada's beacon pinging every relay in the system. The maneuver works but burns out half the ship. Emotional beat: trust made physical.

chapters.title: Voss at the Airlock
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Voss boards during repairs under a parley flag and makes his real offer: Ada is alive, held in consortium custody, traded for the beacon core. Coral wavers until Juno shows her the fabrication markers in the 'proof' — but doubt takes root. Emotional beat: the temptation to buy back the past.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, quiet chapter. Aboard the limping ship, Coral tends a single smuggled seedling from the garden, and she and Juno finally speak plainly about grief, mothers, and the difference between inheritance and obligation. Coral decides: the message goes to everyone, not to any buyer. Emotional beat: choosing principle over rescue.

chapters.title: The Relay at Ceres
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. The neutral relay station braces as Earth and Belt fleets converge. Station master Ilsa Reyes declares the relay open to all parties, gambling that transparency is the only neutrality left. Sefu receives word that the courier ship is inbound, damaged and burning hard. Emotional beat: hope arriving like artillery.

chapters.title: Running the Blockade
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. The Long Patience threads between Earth picket lines and Belt squadrons, both sides trying to seize rather than destroy the beacon. Juno flies the best flight of her life; Coral manually broadcasts decoy signals from the beacon to confuse targeting. They breach the cordon, barely. Emotional beat: two people against two navies, winning anyway.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax part one. At the relay, Coral jacks the beacon core into the station's system-wide array. Voss's strike team breaches the dock; Juno holds the corridor. Ada's full archive floods every channel in the system: the forged attack, the manufactured war, the names of those who profited. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: The Price of the Message
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax part two. Consortium command orders the relay destroyed with all hands; the firing solution is broadcast live, and Earth crews refuse the order en masse. Voss, exposed, tries to kill Coral personally; Juno takes a wound shielding her, and Coral kills Voss with the station's cargo manipulator. The beacon core burns out forever. Emotional beat: survival without triumph.

chapters.title: Ceasefire, Reluctant
chapters.summary: Sefu's POV. Fleets stand down amid mutinies and arrests; the war doesn't end so much as collapse under the weight of evidence. Sefu meets Coral face to face and asks what she wants as restitution. She asks for nothing for herself — only that the seed vault be funded and crewed. Emotional beat: grief finding a shape forward.

chapters.title: Testimony of a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The tribunal plays Ada's final addendum publicly; Coral learns her mother recorded it knowing she might already be gone, addressed to 'whoever my daughter has become.' Coral testifies not about the conspiracy but about the garden — why someone should tend things for people not yet born. Emotional beat: private sorrow becoming public meaning.

chapters.title: Return to Kepler-442c
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Months later, Coral and a recovering Juno return to the garden, now slated to receive actual colonists. The automated systems kept everything alive. Coral plants the smuggled seedling in open ground and decommissions the silent beacon with a salute. Emotional beat: home redefined as something shared.

chapters.title: A Static for the Gravity
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Coral's POV with a closing letter to Ada. As the first new settlers' ship makes orbit, gravity flickers again — nine seconds, harmless, the system's old scar tissue — and this time Coral laughs instead of fearing. She writes: I stayed invisible for eleven years, and it turns out I was always the message. Emotional beat: peace earned, inheritance accepted.
